source.title: Resolution of Some Open Problems Concerning Multiple Zeta Evaluations of Arbitrary Depth

accepted.question_text: Fix a positive integer k. For which positive-integer tuples (s1, ..., sk) does the multiple zeta value ζ(s1, ..., sk) belong to the polynomial ring Q[Z_k], where Z_k denotes the set of all multiple zeta values of depth less than k? Equivalently, which depth-k multiple zeta values can be reduced by rational polynomial relations to values of strictly smaller depth?
accepted.context_brief: General depth-reduction problem for multiple zeta values

evidence.quote: For each positive integer k, let Zk denote the set of all multiple zeta values (with positive integer arguments) of depth less than k. If we restrict our attention to rational polynomial relationships, the aforementioned problem amounts to determining for each k the values of the arguments s1, . . . , sk for which the sum (1) lies in the polynomial ring Q[Zk]. Settling this question in complete generality is currently well beyond the reach of number theory.

accepted.question_text: Is the Riemann zeta value ζ(5) irrational? In the paper's depth-reduction language, is it true that ζ(5) does not lie in Q[Z_1] = Q?

evidence.quote: For example, there is as yet no proof that ζ(5) ∈/ Q[Z1] = Q, although it is strongly suspected that ζ(5) is indeed irrational.

needs_review.question_text_raw: The introduction says high-precision computation led to several beautiful conjectures concerning arbitrary depth reductions [4, 5, 6], but the paper does not restate those conjectures there.

evidence.quote: Additionally, high-precision evaluation of specific multiple zeta values combined with human-directed computer searches using lattice basis reduction algorithms led to several beautiful conjectures concerning arbitrary depth reductions [4, 5, 6].
